'''''Goeppertia veitchiana''''' (syn. ''Calathea veitchiana'') is a species of flowering plant in the [[Marantaceae]] family. It is [[Endemism|endemic]] to [[Ecuador]].<ref name="77130077-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77130077-1 |title=''Goeppertia veitchiana'' (Veitch ex Hook.f.) Borchs. & S.Suárez |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=12 May 2021 }}</ref> Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist [[montane forest]]s.

The plant was discovered near [[Cuenca, Ecuador|Cuenca]] by the [[Victorian era|Victorian]] [[plant collector]] [[Richard Pearce (botanist)|Richard Pearce]] in 1862, and named in honour of his employers, [[James Veitch & Sons]].<ref name = "HV47">{{cite book |author=James Herbert Veitch |title=Hortus Veitchii |publisher=[[Caradoc Doy]] |year=2006 |edition=reprint |page=47 |isbn=0-9553515-0-2 |author-link=James Herbert Veitch |title-link=Hortus Veitchii }}</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Goeppertia veitchiana inflorescence.jpg|left|thumb|192x192px|Inflorescence of ''Goeppertia veitchiana'' ]]
'''''Goeppertia vetichiana''''' is a medium sized plant with wide, ovale, glossy green [[Leaf|leaves]]. It has long, thin [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] and a long [[pulvinus]]. The back of the leaves are often purple. There is a pattern on the upper side of the leaf which makes it very recognizable. It is composed of one wide green band in the middle, with two smaller dark green bands on the edges and with another, two light green bands on each sides of the dark green ones. The [[inflorescence]] of ''G.{{nbsp}}veitchiana'' is similar to ''[[Goeppertia roseopicta]]'', but the bracts are very hairy. The bracts can be purple or green and the [[Flower|flowers]] are white with often two purple staminodes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Curtis |first=William |date=1865 |title= Curtis's botanical magazine|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/439270 |journal=Curtis's Botanical Magazine |volume=91 |pages=5535}}</ref>

== Similar species ==
In 1983, a new species of ''Calathea'' was described from Peru, that, although not closely related to ''C.{{nbsp}}veitchiana'', shows the same leaf pattern and had been previously misidentified in collections as ''C.{{nbsp}}veitchiana''. This new species was named ''Calathea pseudoveitchiana'', and is now ''[[Goeppertia pseudoveitchiana]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |title=A pattern mimic of ''Calathea veitchiana'' from Peru (Marantaceae) |author1=Helen Kennedy |author1-link=Helen Kennedy (botanist) |journal=Canadian Journal of Botany |year=1983 |volume=61 |issue=5 |pages=1429–1434 |doi=10.1139/b83-154}}</ref>
